title: Collect proof of your California address
description: The DMV asks for documents that show you live in California when you apply for a driver license. Without them the office visit does not count, so this comes before the license.
steps: Open the DMV's list of accepted residency documents.
Pick documents that show your name and new California address, such as a signed lease or a utility bill.
Keep the originals together with your identity document for the DMV visit.
documents: California residency documents from the DMV's accepted list
Identity document from the DMV's accepted list

source.name: California DMV — Requirements for a California driver's license

title: Get a California driver license
description: If you become a California resident and drive, the DMV says you must get a California driver license within 10 days.
steps: Start the driver license application on the DMV site.
Book a DMV office visit.
Bring your identity and residency documents and your current license.
documents: Identity and California residency documents listed by the DMV

deadline.label: Within 10 days of becoming a California resident

financial.note: The DMV charges an application fee.

source.name: California DMV — Requirements for a California driver's license

title: Move your auto insurance to a California policy
description: California's minimum liability limits rose on January 1, 2025: $30,000 for injury or death of one person, $60,000 per accident, and $15,000 for property damage.
steps: Tell your insurer your move date and California garaging address.
Confirm the new policy meets the 30/60/15 minimum.
Keep proof of insurance for your DMV registration visit.

financial.note: Your premium is re-rated for the new address.

source.name: California Department of Insurance — Automobile insurance guide

title: Register your vehicle in California
description: The California DMV requires a vehicle from another state to be registered within 20 days of establishing residency or accepting employment in California. The DMV advises submitting the application and fees on time even if some paperwork is still missing.
steps: Get a smog certification from a California smog station, if your vehicle needs one.
Complete form REG 343, signed by every registered owner.
Bring the vehicle to a DMV office for VIN verification (REG 31). An appointment is recommended.
Hand in the out-of-state title, registration and plates, and pay the fees.

deadline.label: Within 20 days of establishing residency or accepting employment in California

financial.note: Registration fees and use tax are due. Late registration adds DMV penalties.

source.name: California DMV — New California resident portal

title: Enroll through Covered California
description: A Marketplace plan from another state does not follow you. Moving to California is a qualifying life event, and Covered California generally gives you 60 days from the move date to apply.
steps: Start a new application at CoveredCA.com with your California address.
Compare plans available in your new ZIP code.
Pick a plan, then end your old-state plan so the coverage dates line up.
documents: Proof of your new address and move date (lease, utility bill)
Social Security numbers for everyone applying

deadline.label: Generally 60 days from the date of your move

financial.note: Miss the window and you wait for the next open enrollment without a plan.

title: Review your quarterly estimated tax payments
description: With 1099 or self-employment income, no employer withholds tax for you. The IRS says you generally have to make estimated payments if you expect to owe $1,000 or more when you file.
steps: Estimate this year's income and tax with the Form 1040-ES worksheet.
Pay each quarter through IRS Direct Pay or your IRS online account.
Check whether California also expects state estimated payments.

deadline.label: Quarterly: April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15 (next business day if the date falls on a weekend or holiday)

financial.note: Underpaying a quarter can add an IRS underpayment penalty.

title: Enroll your child in a California school
description: In California, children between 6 and 18 are subject to compulsory full-time education. A child is admitted to kindergarten if they turn five on or before September 1 of the school year.
steps: Find the school district for your new address.
Ask the district for its enrollment document list.
Bring your child's immunization record to registration.
Request records from the previous school.
documents: Immunization record (checked at admission under California Department of Public Health rules)
Other documents on your school district's enrollment list

deadline.label: Before your child's first school day after the move

source.name: California Department of Education — Kindergarten FAQ

title: Tell the IRS your new address
description: The IRS mails notices and refunds to the address it has on file. Form 8822 updates your home mailing address.
steps: Download Form 8822 from IRS.gov.
Fill in your old and new address.
Mail it to the IRS address listed in the form instructions for your old state.

financial.note: A missed IRS notice can turn into late-payment interest.

title: Plan for a California part-year resident return
description: If you move into California during the year, the Franchise Tax Board treats you as a part-year resident. Part-year residents who meet the income thresholds file Form 540NR.
steps: Write down the exact date you became a California resident.
Keep pay records split by before and after the move.
At tax time, file Form 540NR with Schedule CA (540NR).
documents: W-2s and 1099s for the full year

deadline.label: Filed with your state return for the year of the move

financial.note: California taxes all income received while you are a resident.

source.name: California FTB — Part-year resident and nonresident

title: Give your employer a California DE 4
description: The federal W-4 only covers federal withholding. California income tax withholding is set by the state DE 4. Without a valid DE 4, an employer withholds as single with zero allowances.
steps: Download the DE 4 from the EDD site.
Complete it with your filing status and allowances.
Hand it to your employer's payroll team together with your new address.

financial.note: Wrong state withholding shows up as a bill or an oversized refund at tax time.

title: Check whether Texas expects a final state return
description: States that tax income usually want a part-year return for the months you lived there. Civio has not verified the rule for Texas.
steps: Open the Texas tax agency site from the official directory.
Look for part-year resident filing rules.
Note the form name and due date in this task.

financial.note: Income earned before the move may be taxable in Texas.

verificationNote: Civio has no verified rule for this state yet. Confirm the requirement and any deadline on the official site before acting.
